title: ChatGPT Ads as over 100k advertisers have used the platform
content:
ChatGPT Ads expands to 26 new countries as over 100,000 advertisers have used the platform
From local businesses to global brands, more advertisers can now reach people as they explore, compare and decide what to buy in ChatGPT.
More than 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week to explore ideas, compare options and make decisions. Ads can help people discover products and services that fit their needs, including options they might not have found otherwise.
Since we launched ads just over eight months ago, over 100,000 advertisers have run campaigns on ChatGPT. Today, we’re expanding ChatGPT Ads to 26 additional countries, extending availability to 89 countries worldwide. This launch builds on our recent expansions across Europe and Southeast Asia and Taiwan.
Advertising helps support free and low-cost access to ChatGPT for people around the world. Our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. Ads will appear only on the Free and Go plans. Plus, Pro, and Enterprise subscriptions will remain ad-free.
Following our launches in Mexico and Brazil, we’re bringing ChatGPT Ads to 14 more Latin American countries, including Argentina, Chile, Colombia, and Peru. We’re also launching in more markets across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia, including Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Cambodia, Bangladesh, and Pakistan.
Advertisers can access ChatGPT Ads in these countries through technology partners or self-service access through Ads Manager(opens in a new window).
In ChatGPT, people can explain what they’re looking for, ask follow-up questions, and refine their options through conversation. Someone training for their first marathon might start by exploring meal ideas for race week, then narrow their options based on their dietary preferences and how much time they have to cook. An ad relevant to that conversation could introduce them to a grocery delivery service they hadn’t considered.
For local businesses, regional brands, and international companies, ChatGPT Ads gives businesses a way to introduce their products during these moments of consideration, when people are still evaluating their options and deciding what’s right for them.
Protecting the trust people place in ChatGPT is foundational to our approach to advertising.
Guided by OpenAI’s ads principles, we keep conversations private from advertisers and do not sell customer data. Ads in ChatGPT are clearly labeled and separate from ChatGPT’s answers, and advertising does not influence the answers ChatGPT provides.
Our goal is to make ads useful to people as they pursue their goals and make decisions—and effective for the businesses that advertise with us.
Our focus remains expanding access to AI while staying true to our principles.
With ChatGPT Ads now available in 89 countries, our next phase of growth will include the development of additional formats, objectives, buying options, and measurement capabilities. We are also continuing to explore new ways for businesses to interact with consumers in more native ways in ChatGPT.
As more people turn to ChatGPT to explore needs, evaluate options, and make decisions, we see an opportunity to help them discover products and services—and to help businesses of every size grow and thrive.
Businesses interested in advertising on ChatGPT can learn more at ads.openai.com(opens in a new window).

report.summary: OpenAI expands ChatGPT Ads to 26 more countries, reaching 89 markets, after more than 100,000 advertisers used the platform in its first eight months.
report.background: ChatGPT Ads launched just over eight months ago as OpenAI looked for ways to support free and low-cost access to its assistant, which now serves more than 1.2 billion weekly users. The expansion follows earlier rollouts in Mexico, Brazil, Europe, Southeast Asia and Taiwan. It reflects a broader shift in the AI industry: assistants are becoming discovery and shopping surfaces, not just answer engines. That puts ChatGPT in competition with search engines, social platforms and retail media for advertiser budgets. At the same time, OpenAI is trying to reassure users that advertising will not compromise conversation privacy or answer quality. Ads appear only on Free and Go plans; Plus, Pro and Enterprise remain ad-free.
key_points: OpenAI is adding 26 countries, bringing ChatGPT Ads to 89 markets. New markets include 14 more Latin American countries such as Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru, plus Nigeria, South Africa, Serbia, Ukraine, Cambodia, Bangladesh and Pakistan. Advertisers can buy through technology partners or self-service Ads Manager.

More than 100,000 advertisers have run campaigns since launch just over eight months ago. OpenAI says ChatGPT has 1.2 billion weekly users who explore, compare and decide what to buy, making the assistant an attractive place for brands to reach people during consideration moments.

Ads appear only on ChatGPT Free and Go plans. Plus, Pro and Enterprise subscriptions stay ad-free. OpenAI says advertising helps fund free and low-cost access, positioning ads as a monetization layer rather than a feature for paying customers.

OpenAI says conversations remain private from advertisers, customer data is not sold, ads are clearly labeled and separated from answers, and advertising does not influence ChatGPT’s responses. These promises are meant to protect user trust as ads scale across 89 countries.

OpenAI plans additional ad formats, objectives, buying options and measurement capabilities, and will explore more native ways for businesses to interact with consumers in ChatGPT. That signals ads are becoming a core product area, not a one-off experiment.
report.impact: ChatGPT Ads signals that AI assistants are becoming ad-supported discovery platforms, similar to search and social feeds. For the AI industry, it creates a new revenue stream and a competitive threat to search advertising, retail media and social commerce. Developers should watch whether ad formats, measurement APIs or marketplace integrations emerge, and whether free-tier economics change. For regular users, the trade-off is clearer: more ads on free and low-cost plans, but paid tiers stay ad-free. Trust will depend on whether ads remain labeled, separate from answers and uninfluenced by advertisers. If OpenAI can preserve answer quality and privacy, conversational ads could become a mainstream channel; if not, they risk eroding confidence in AI assistants.
report.tools: Watch OpenAI’s Ads Manager and ads.openai.com for campaign setup, country availability and future formats. For privacy-friendly measurement, advertisers can explore open-source analytics such as Matomo, Plausible and PostHog to track traffic and conversions without selling user data. Also follow OpenAI’s ads principles for policy updates.
